lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Body Signals and Building a Fueling Meal
lessonRef.title: Application or project: planning and ingredient checks

objective: Learners independently plan a simple no-heat meal for a specific day, checking real (or provided) ingredient availability against their plan, and revise the plan for any missing ingredient.
scenario: The learner plans out one no-heat meal they intend to actually build later, checks the ingredients they planned against what's really available (in the kitchen or a provided inventory), and revises the plan for anything missing rather than assuming it'll be there.
safetyNotes: This is a planning-and-checking task, not food preparation; no heat or sharp tools are used.

simulationAlternative.description: If checking a real kitchen's ingredients isn't available, the learner instead checks their draft plan against a provided sample ingredient inventory list, revising for any 'missing' item the same way as the guided task.

materials: access to the kitchen or a provided ingredient inventory

tasks.directions: Before checking availability, write your first-draft meal plan: what ingredients would you use if everything were available?
Check your planned ingredients against what's actually available (in your kitchen or a provided list), with an adult confirming what's really on hand.

prompts.text: I checked every ingredient on my draft plan, not just the ones I assumed were there.
For each missing ingredient, I named a specific substitute or removed it from the plan.
My revised plan only uses ingredients that are actually available.

tasks.directions: Write your final, checked meal plan in a form ready to use later.

prompts.text: List your final ingredients and note which ones changed from your first draft, and why.
What's one thing you learned from this check that you'll do differently the next time you plan a meal — checking earlier, planning backup ingredients, or something else?

remediation: If the learner's revised plan still assumes an unavailable ingredient, reteach by having them physically point to or list each ingredient's real location (or its absence) one at a time before finalizing the plan.
extension: Plan a second meal for a different day using only ingredients that are currently available, without needing a first-draft revision step.
